title: Microsoft Teams: separate invites for town hall attendees, presenters and co-organizers
notes: claim 49: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The roadmap facts, Message Center rollout windows and both published control paths are supported. Corrections should qualify the data-access assurance and rollout wording, acknowledge the existing Teams events licensing, and cite the policy reference with its preview qualification.

claims.claim: This roadmap change is for Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a backend change separating attendee invites from the events crew.
claims.quote: This backend change will now address the 'separation of attendee' invites from the events crew.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor MC1009930 names a licence or meter for this change.
claims.quote: Searched: licence, license, meter and prerequisites in the supplied roadmap record and complete MC1009930 post; neither names a licence or meter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published licensing specific to separated town hall invites.
claims.quote: All eligible Teams licenses include the foundational capabilities needed to create and run events, engage attendees, review attendance reports, and publish event recordings.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the licensing notes with 'Teams events are included in eligible licences, including Office 365 E3 and Microsoft 365 E3. Microsoft has not published licensing specific to role-separated invites.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing. In Cost and licensing and the cost rationale, replace the blanket unpublished-licensing statement with 'No licensing specific to role-separated invites is published.'

claims.claim: Plan for Teams events states that an Attendee Capacity Pack add-on licence allows organizers to scale events up to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: With an Attendee Capacity Pack add-on license, organizers can scale events up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said that the event capacity add-on relates to the invite-separation change.
claims.quote: Searched: "town hall" "separate" "invites" "license". Read Plan for Teams events, Teams events licensing overview, the roadmap and MC1009930; none connects the capacity add-on to role-separated invites.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin UI or API switch is documented for choosing whether the role-separated invite behaviour is used.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams town hall separated invites admin switch PowerShell disable separation role emails. Read Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy, Manage email communications, Plan for Teams events and Graph town hall API use cases; none documents a separation switch.

claims.claim: The email-editing control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Customize event emails.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Turn the Customize event emails toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEmailEditing Disabled turns off event email-template editing.
claims.quote:
The following example turns off -AllowEmailEditing so organizers and co-organizers can't edit email templates:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEmailEditing Disabled
claims.fix: Keep the command. Add 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference labels this policy as preview' to controls[1].note and the rendered row note. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps, which says 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.' The email-management guide does not state that qualification.

claims.claim: The event email-editing policy has user-level scope.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps to sources; keep the user scope.

claims.claim: The existing control determines whether organizers and co-organizers can edit event email templates.
claims.quote: You can control whether event organizers and co-organizers can edit email templates for their events.

claims.claim: The event email page lists the templates organizers and co-organizers can edit.
claims.quote:
Organizers and co-organizers can edit the following email communication templates:
- Registration confirmation
- Pending approval
- Waitlisting
- Registration rejected
- Registration cancellation
- Event cancellation
- Date and time update
- Event reminder
- Event recording available

claims.claim: The domain used to send event emails can be configured in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can configure this setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center by selecting a verified domain for sending system notifications.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that Customize event emails covers the newly separated invites.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "town hall" "separate invites". Read Manage email communications, Plan for Teams events and the policy reference; the listed editable templates do not identify the new role-separated invitations.

claims.claim: The documented email-editing and sender-domain controls govern templates and the sending domain, rather than separation of invites by recipient role.
claims.quote:
You can control whether event organizers and co-organizers can edit email templates for their events.
You can also configure the domain used to send event emails.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this particular roadmap change.
claims.quote: Searched: "476488"; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "town hall" "separate invites". Read Plan for Teams events, Manage email communications and Graph town hall API use cases; no feature-specific description found.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap and notice do not specify the complete contents of each invite or how roles are represented within it.
claims.quote: Searched: invite contents and role representation in the complete roadmap description and MC1009930. The notice describes an organizer email explaining participant roles, but supplies no full template or invite-field details.

claims.claim: No new data source is described in the supplied feature notices.
claims.quote: This backend change will now address the 'separation of attendee' invites from the events crew. This feature allows the organizers of Townhalls to maintain separate invites for attendees.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor MC1009930 says this change alters who can attend or present.
claims.quote: Searched: attendance and presenter eligibility changes in the supplied roadmap record and complete MC1009930; both describe invitation separation, not changes to attendance or presentation permissions.

claims.claim: The notice describes participant invitations rather than any additional autonomous action on a user's behalf.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams Events invite emails will be separated based on the role of the participant.

claims.claim: The roadmap and supplied notice name no prerequisite or required administrator role for this rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: prerequisites and required administrator roles in the supplied roadmap record and complete MC1009930; neither specifies them, and MC1009930 says no admin action is required.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The changed invitations arrive from January 2027.
claims.quote:
Targeted Release: We will begin rolling out early January 2027
General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High): We will begin rolling out mid-January 2027
claims.fix: In the summary replace 'Rolls out automatically from January 2027' with 'Automatic rollout is expected to begin in January 2027'. In Why it matters, Before rollout and the impact rationale, replace 'from January 2027' with 'with rollout expected to begin in January 2027'. Keep the detailed attributed notice windows unchanged.

claims.claim: The change adds no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams town hall separate role invitations new data access security permissions change. Read the roadmap, MC1009930, Plan for Teams events, Manage email communications and Graph town hall API use cases; none establishes that data access is unchanged.
claims.fix: Replace 'adds no new data access' with 'describes no new data access' in the risk rationale, matching the body's narrower description of what the notices say.
